repo_prior_art.cite: none; no Hawkes/fixed-bin exact-identification proposal appears in the catalogue

published_prior_art.cite: BacryMuzy2016 uses full second-order functions; EtesamiZhangSinghalKiyavash2016 uses full spectral/Laplace information; Koyama2025 gives a small-bin coarse-graining approximation; ZhouPapadogeorgou2025 uses the full aggregated-count law.
The independent-Poisson consequence of a zero Hawkes kernel is standard; no cited source gives this exact fixed-bin boundary characterization.
Hawkes1971Spectra and BacryMuzy2016 retain first-order intensity; AchabBacryGaiffasMastromatteoMuzy2017 uses higher cumulants.
CheyssonLang2022 supplies binned Whittle asymptotics, but not the random-image restricted-logarithm inverse.
WangXieCuozzoMakXie2020 and WangKolarShojaie2025 provide exact-event-time network inference rather than fixed-bin covariance-inverse coverage.
No located fixed-bin Hawkes result characterizes the one-positive-lag injectivity fiber on a nondegenerate legal region.
No located Hawkes confidence procedure characterizes joint honest graph-and-parameter adaptation through rank, weak-edge, and empty-network boundaries.

novelty_flags.label: thm:two-lag-exact-recovery
novelty_flags.one_line: Add Kirchner2016, Hawkes and INAR(∞) Processes, as a close binned-count/lag-structure comparator and distinguish its approximation route from the proposed exact finite-lag inverse.

soundness_flags.label: thm:rank-adaptive-estimation
soundness_flags.one_line: “Converges uniformly to a centered Gaussian law” lacks the probability metric and the precise uniform assertion over the varying covariance family; state a supremum formulation (for example over bounded-Lipschitz test functions) and its uniform HAC conditions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 4–5, Theorem 3 equation (14), Corollary 4, Proposition 6; pp. 8–9, Sections 7.2–7.3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper identifies exponential exciting modes from zeros of the inverse trace of the Fourier-transformed normalized covariance and recovers coefficient matrices using Laplace transforms of the covariance density.
The article studies stationary Hawkes processes observed as fixed-interval counts and states consistency and asymptotic normality for Whittle spectral estimators under a moment condition.

The paper generalizes MC-EM estimation to multivariate binned Hawkes processes and compares it with INAR(p) and binned-likelihood approximations; it does not state a finite-moment identifying inverse.

The paper studies low-resolution discrete-time event sequences, identifies instantaneous-effect ambiguity in ordinary Hawkes/Granger approaches, and proposes Structural Hawkes Processes with an identifiability result.

The published paper is Causal Structure Learning in Hawkes Processes with Complex Latent Confounder Networks; it uses a shrinking-interval discrete-time representation and rank-based conditions for latent-subprocess and causal-influence discovery.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Kirchner2016 to related work and explain why its INAR(∞)/binned-process route neither supplies nor contradicts the exact two-positive-lag inverse.
Replace the informal uniform-CLT wording with a specified distributional metric, a uniform long-run-covariance/HAC consistency claim, and explicit constants controlled by the margin class.
Sharpen the one-lag open question into a worked nondegenerate chain, fork, or diamond fiber theorem before attempting the full stratified locus.

recommended_next_step: Revise the survey around the missing INAR(∞) comparator and formalize the uniform asymptotic assertion, then return the field-tier exact-recovery kernel for review.
